rationale:
ROUND 2. Round 1 (correlation c4d9c841) came back REVISE, gated by `editquality`:
the plan made `--color-accent-text` reachable but shipped no edit that CONSUMED it
for any of the three measured failures it claimed to close. That objection was
correct, and answering it properly meant going and reading the three failing rules
rather than repointing something plausible. Doing so REFUTED my own sub-shape C
framing, so this round is a different plan, not a patched one.

WHAT I ASSERTED IN ROUND 1, AND WHAT THE CODE ACTUALLY SAYS.

I described sub-shape C as "a component hard-coding an ink over a themed fill".
Not one of the three cited rules hard-codes anything. Pulled from the live
`content_components.html_template` and checked against each site's served
stylesheet (browser UA, /assets/css/styles.css), 2026-08-06:

  finetuning.uk `.csg-cta-btn`  (component `case-studies-grid`)
      background: var(--color-accent, var(--color-secondary))   -> #C8873A
      color:      var(--color-primary-text, #fff)               -> #ffffff
      = 3.01:1. The fallback never fires: --color-primary-text IS defined, as
      #ffffff, and it is CORRECT for its own slot — primary is #1A1A2E, so white
      is the right ink ON A PRIMARY FILL. The defect is that the fill here is
      ACCENT. The component names the wrong ink slot. This is precisely what
      `accent_text` was derived for on 2026-07-27, and 0 of 18 layouts declare it,
      so --color-accent-text is absent from all three served stylesheets (grep
      count 0/0/0). THIS is the consumer edit round 1 was missing.

  gaswholesalers.com `.A`  (the base `a {}` rule in the LAYOUT css_template)
      a { color: var(--color-accent); }  -> #E8A020 on white = 2.22:1, x6.
      Not a component and not a hard-coded literal: it is the palette's accent
      used as the page's link ink. `--color-accent-text` is the WRONG repair here
      — that slot is the ink that goes ON an accent fill, the opposite direction.

  gamesdesign.co.uk `.stats-eyebrow`  (component `system-stats`)
      color: var(--color-accent, #7dd3fc)  -> #00e5ff
      background: var(--section-surface)   -> rgba(255,255,255,0.05)
      composited over --color-primary #00bcd4 = rgb(13,191,214). 1.44:1.
      (0.05*255 + 0.95*[0,188,212] = [13,191,214] — the arithmetic identifies the
      ground exactly, which is how I know the section fill is `primary`.)
      Again accent AS an ink, not an ink ON accent.

So the three cited failures are TWO different questions, and round 1 offered one
answer. The correction is that a palette colour needs BOTH directions named:
  --color-<x>-text  = the ink that goes ON an <x> fill      (already derived; unreachable)
  --color-<x>-ink   = <x> itself, made legible AS an ink    (new; this is the gap)
Sub-shape A (`--color-primary` as an ink: dartsonline .image-hover-card-grid__eyebrow
1.04, robot-hands .tl-eyebrow 1.14 / .tl-card-link 1.07) is the primary case of the
second direction and was already in round 1. gaswholesalers and gamesdesign are the
accent case of the same direction, which round 1 misfiled.

A FOURTH SHAPE, FOUND WHILE CHECKING, AND DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS PLAN.

gamesdesign's other 8 failures are `.stat-label`/`.stat-description` at 1.72:1,
rgba(255,255,255,0.7) on the same cyan. That colour is in no stylesheet. It comes
from `system-stats`'s own inline <style>:

      .system-stats-section { --section-text: rgba(255,255,255,0.9);
                              --section-text-muted: rgba(255,255,255,0.7); }

a component redefining tokens the renderer emits with a block that says, in the
served CSS, "Themes MUST NOT declare --section-* defaults; the renderer owns
this." The component's scoped selector beats the renderer's body-level block, so
the renderer's contrast-checked value loses. MEASURED fleet-wide: 47 of 173 active
unforked components declare a renderer-owned --section-* token; 32 do it with a raw
rgb/rgba literal. idea.uk's 14 failures are the same shape (`brief-explanation`
declares its own --section-text-muted, and idea.uk's stylesheet has no
renderer-enforced section block at all).

That is ~22 of the 109 failures and it is a bigger, differently-shaped defect: an
unenforced contract, not a missing variable. It is being filed as its own bug. I am
naming it here because it is the honest answer to "does this plan close the bug" —
it does not, and I would rather say which part it leaves than let the count imply
otherwise. Folding a 47-component contract-enforcement change into this one is
exactly the opportunistic bundling the guardian seat vetoes.

WHAT ELSE CHANGED SINCE ROUND 1, EACH ANSWERING A NAMED OBJECTION.

- debug_historian (HIGH): the migration moves onto the documented ledger —
  docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/324_*.sql, applied by
  scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh, registered in schema_migrations. Round 1
  invented a path. It also gains the needle-gate discipline: a mechanically derived
  pre-count of the exact needle, anchored exact-substring matching via position()
  rather than LIKE (no % to be tripped by), a pg_dump of the affected rows named in
  the header, an inline rollback block, and DO/RAISE assertions on every count —
  because a verify block of bare SELECTs cannot stop a COMMIT.
- bug_historian (HIGH): the render-audit cadence row is now IN this plan (edit 8),
  not deferred. The detector for this exact defect class is live in v1.0.1257 and
  dispatched by nothing; shipping a fix for measured instances while leaving the
  class's own detector dark is the pattern this council exists to catch, and the
  objection was right. The pre-fix baseline it verifies against is banked.
- bug_historian + guardian (MEDIUM, both): the call-order dependency now has a test
  that FAILS if buildLegibleInkDefaults is moved before buildTokenAliases (edit 6),
  not a comment asserting the order. A positional invariant with no positive
  assertion was correctly called containable-but-real.
- render_guardian (MEDIUM): the plan now names the propagation step and its
  verification — the template edit reaches a visitor only through a rerender, and
  the check is the served page, not the migration's row count.
- editquality (MEDIUM): the cascade-drop failure mode is ruled out by construction
  and pinned by test case 5. Every consumer is written as
  var(--color-X-ink, <exactly what is there today>), so an undefined new variable
  resolves to today's bytes. The var(--spacing-*) case that landmine describes drops
  the declaration because its fallback is EMPTY; none of these have an empty
  fallback.
- guardian (MEDIUM): the owning pipeline (brochure_component_library) is named in
  the edit block itself, not in the risks prose.
- prior_art_librarian (LOW): I read the two bodies rather than describing them.
  pickInkOn (palette_specialised_slots.go:288) takes ONE bg, walks
  {text, background, text_muted}, and can never return the source colour — it exists
  to find an ink for a fill it is handed. pickReadableOnBackground (color_util.go:134)
  takes ONE bg and walks paletteTextPreference for section body copy. Neither can
  answer "is THIS colour legible, and if not what is the nearest palette colour that
  is, across N grounds at once", and neither has a source-unchanged branch. Extending
  either would change what its existing callers get. legibleInkFor is a third
  function because it is a third question, and I checked that by reading, not by
  signature.
- architecture (LOW): the scheme-widening fork is recorded in the concept-register
  entry that ships in the same commit, with the reason a future narrowing would
  silently stop covering the light-site cases.

STILL UNRESOLVED AND NOT CLAIMED. ai-agent-orchestration.com's 30 failures
(--color-heading resolving to its own background) went to the 090 diagnosis loop
and came back UNVERIFIABLE — "Diagnosis NOT confirmed (stopped: iteration-cap)".
Five bundles, no cause. It is untouched here and needs a human. vonc.com's 23
gauntlet failures remain with the gauntlet_dead_cta lane. This plan closes the
sub-shape A and the accent-direction failures: 1 dartsonline, 2 robot-hands,
2 finetuning, 6 gaswholesalers, 1 gamesdesign, and .stats-eyebrow on vonc.

plan.summary: Name both directions of the ink question. A palette colour used as a FILL already has a derived ink that goes on it (`accent_text`, derived since 2026-07-27, declared by 0 of 18 layouts, therefore never emitted to one stylesheet). A palette colour used as an INK on the page has nothing — and that is the gap behind every failure this plan closes. Emit three companions from the CSS renderer's own :root block, after the token aliases: --color-primary-ink and --color-accent-ink (the colour itself when it clears AA against every ground it lands on, else the nearest palette colour that does), and --color-accent-text (the existing dead derivation, made reachable). Then opt the measured offenders in: 4 shared components and the base `a {}` rule in 5 layouts, each written var(--new, <exactly today's value>) so an un-rendered stylesheet is byte-identical. Emission is renderer-owned rather than added to 18 layout css_templates because a palette slot no layout declares is never emitted, and it is scheme-independent unlike fillDarkSchemeSpecialisedSlots because 2 of the 3 accent-direction sites are LIGHT. Ships with the render-audit cadence row so the detector for this class stops being dark.

edits.rationale: The question 'is this colour legible as text on EVERY ground it lands on, and if not what is the nearest palette colour that is' is answered nowhere. I read the two candidates rather than inferring from signatures. pickInkOn (:288) walks {text, background, text_muted} against ONE bg and structurally cannot return the colour it was asked about — it finds an ink for a fill. pickReadableOnBackground (color_util.go:134) walks paletteTextPreference against ONE bg for section body copy. Neither has a source-unchanged branch and neither takes multiple grounds; adding either would change what today's callers receive. Requiring ALL grounds is the load-bearing part: dartsonline places the same ink on the page background (.image-hover-card-grid__eyebrow, 1.04) and on the derived card_bg (.tl-card-link, 1.07 on robot-hands), so a single-ground version would fix whichever page I happened to test and leave the other failing.

The seam. THREE variables, not two — this is the round-1 correction. Reading the three cited rules showed they are two different questions: case-studies-grid puts an ink ON an accent fill (needs accent_text, which exists and is unreachable), while the layouts' `a {}` and system-stats' .stats-eyebrow use accent AS an ink (needs accent-ink, which does not exist). Round 1 offered only the first and so could not have fixed gaswholesalers or gamesdesign, which is exactly what editquality said. Renderer-owned rather than 18 layout css_templates because a slot no layout declares is never emitted; skips any name the CSS already defines, as buildTokenAliases does, so a theme with an opinion keeps it.

warnUnusablePrimary already measures the exact condition the new slot repairs, and its own comment justifies warning-not-failing with 'there is no single correct repair'. That stopped being true in this change. A warning that names no remedy makes the next reader re-derive the whole analysis — this bug is nine days old and that is roughly what happened. Kept deliberately as a WARN, not promoted to an error: the palette author's fill-vs-foreground decision is still theirs.

Wire the block in as step 12. It MUST run after steps 10 and 11, because it tests the assembled CSS for an existing definition of each name; running it earlier lets a later block define the name and win, producing a variable that is emitted and inert — the dead-config outcome this change exists to remove. Round 1 stated that dependency in a comment and both bug_historian and guardian objected that a positional invariant with no assertion is not an invariant. Edit 6 asserts it.

Six cases, each chosen to fail a plausible wrong implementation rather than to cover lines. Case 2 is the one that matters most and is the reason this is not a one-line change: a fix that repaints sites whose colours are already legible is a regression wearing a win. Each assertion will be proven load-bearing by deleting the branch it guards and confirming a DISTINCT failure message — a test that still passes when the rule is gone is not a test, and a mutation that passes may have hit a guard in series, so the message has to be the specific one.

The positional assertion bug_historian and guardian both asked for, as a test rather than a comment. Round 1's answer to 'what stops a later edit reordering this' was a comment, and the objection — that this recreates the dead-config landmine one layer up, moving the fragility from layout-declaration to call-order without removing it — is right. This fails loudly on a reorder.

OWNING PIPELINE: brochure_component_library owns content_components.html_template; the layouts rows are owned by the same pipeline's theme half. Named here at the edit, per the guardian's objection, rather than in the risks prose. ON THE LEDGER this time (docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents/NNN_, run by scripts/migration/run-migrations.sh, registered in schema_migrations) — round 1 invented a path outside it, which debug_historian flagged HIGH and was right to: a migration number is not yours because you named a file. Number confirmed free against the ledger immediately before applying, not when writing. Six repoints closing 12 measured failures: case-studies-grid .csg-cta-btn + .csg-filter-btn.active (finetuning, 2), system-stats .stats-eyebrow (gamesdesign 1, vonc 1), image-hover-card-grid __eyebrow (dartsonline 1), tool-list .tl-eyebrow + .tl-card-link (robot-hands 2), and the base `a {}` rule in the 5 layouts that colour it with accent (gaswholesalers 6). PROPAGATION, per render_guardian: a template edit reaches a visitor only through a rerender, so the migration ends by listing the affected page_components and the verification is the SERVED page, not the row count.
edits.sketch:
-- 324_components_opt_into_legible_ink_slots.sql
--
-- Every replacement is var(<new>, <EXACTLY WHAT IS THERE TODAY>), so a page
-- whose stylesheet predates the renderer change renders byte-identically:
--
--   case-studies-grid  .csg-cta-btn, .csg-filter-btn.active
--     color: var(--color-primary-text, #fff)
--       ->   color: var(--color-accent-text, var(--color-primary-text, #fff))
--     (the fill is var(--color-accent,…); primary-text is the wrong slot)
--   system-stats  .stats-eyebrow
--     color: var(--color-accent, #7dd3fc)
--       ->   color: var(--color-accent-ink, var(--color-accent, #7dd3fc))
--   image-hover-card-grid __eyebrow / tool-list .tl-eyebrow,.tl-card-link
--     color: var(--color-primary)
--       ->   color: var(--color-primary-ink, var(--color-primary))
--   layouts (5 of 18)  a { color: var(--color-accent); }
--       ->   a { color: var(--color-accent-ink, var(--color-accent)); }
--
-- NEEDLE GATE. Not LIKE — position() on the exact substring, so there is no %
-- to be tripped by and no anchoring to get wrong:
--
--   \copy (SELECT id,name,html_template FROM content_components WHERE name IN (...))
--     TO 'backup_324_content_components.tsv'      -- named in this header; taken first
--
--   DO $$
--   DECLARE need int; got int;
--   BEGIN
--     -- derive the count mechanically; do not assert a number I typed
--     SELECT count(*) INTO need FROM content_components
--       WHERE name='case-studies-grid'
--         AND position('var(--color-primary-text, #fff)' in html_template) > 0;
--     IF need = 0 THEN
--       RAISE EXCEPTION 'needle absent in case-studies-grid — the template moved '
--         'under this migration; STOP and re-read it rather than widening the match';
--     END IF;
--     UPDATE content_components SET html_template = replace(html_template,
--              'var(--color-primary-text, #fff)',
--              'var(--color-accent-text, var(--color-primary-text, #fff))'),
--            updated_at = now()
--      WHERE name='case-studies-grid';
--     GET DIAGNOSTICS got = ROW_COUNT;
--     IF got <> need THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'expected % rows, updated %', need, got; END IF;
--     -- and the post-state, which a SELECT cannot enforce:
--     PERFORM 1 FROM content_components WHERE name='case-studies-grid'
--       AND position('var(--color-accent-text,' in html_template) > 0;
--     IF NOT FOUND THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'post-state missing; rolling back'; END IF;
--   END $$;
--
-- ...repeated per component. A verify block of bare SELECTs CANNOT stop the
-- COMMIT — ON_ERROR_STOP ignores a non-empty result — so every check is
-- DO/RAISE, and each RAISE is induced once against a scratch copy to prove it
-- actually fires.
--
-- ROLLBACK: the inverse replace(), same DO/RAISE shape, at the foot of the file
-- behind a commented guard, plus the .tsv above.
--
-- PROPAGATION (render_guardian). The UPDATE changes the SOURCE. The visitor
-- sees it only after a scoped rerender of the affected sections:
--   SELECT s.domain, p.url, cc.name FROM page_components pc JOIN ... ;
--   -- 1 image-hover-card-grid, 6 tool-list, + case-studies-grid/system-stats
-- Verification is the served page re-audited, NOT this file's row counts and
-- NOT a 'complete' work item.

edits.rationale: bug_historian's HIGH objection, answered by inclusion rather than by deferral. The whole detection chain for this defect class is live in v1.0.1257 — write_render_audit_findings pod-grepped at 11 occurrences against an invented control of 0, and render-audit-agent's live row carries site->audit->write_findings->complete — and 0 of 28 enabled scheduled_tasks target it. Total contrast_failure items ever raised: 4, all relojistas.com, all 2026-08-04, i.e. one hand-run. Shipping a fix for six measured instances while the detector that would catch the seventh stays dark is bugs_open/083 / 093 / 115 one more time, and the seat was right that 'detected but undispatched' is indistinguishable from 'fixed' until the next site regresses. The pre-fix baseline is banked (15 sites, 109 failures, 2026-08-06) so the first scheduled run is a comparison, not a first sighting.
edits.sketch:
-- 325_render_audit_gets_a_cadence.sql
--
-- One row. \d scheduled_tasks first — column names read, not assumed.
--
-- INSERT INTO scheduled_tasks (name, target_agent_type, enabled, schedule, ...)
-- VALUES ('render-audit-fleet-weekly', 'render-audit-agent', true, <weekly>, ...)
-- ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING;
--
-- WEEKLY, not daily, and the reason is in this bug's own history: findings
-- dedupe on contrast_failure:<page-path>#<selector>, and a falling failure
-- count is NOT evidence of repair — it is content-dependent (122's dartsonline
-- round found the same defect reporting 1 or 2 depending which cards a page
-- rendered). A daily cadence multiplies that noise without adding signal.
--
-- DO/RAISE assertions, because this is the edit whose silent failure mode is
-- worst — a disabled or mistyped row looks exactly like a working one:
--   1. target_agent_type matches a live agent_definitions row (a task pointing
--      at a nonexistent agent enqueues and dies quietly).
--   2. exactly one enabled row targets render-audit-agent afterwards.
--   3. enabled IS TRUE — asserted, not assumed from the INSERT.
--
-- VERIFICATION IS NOT THIS FILE. It is: the task fires; an orchestration row
-- appears for render-audit-agent; contrast_failure work items are raised whose
-- count and selectors line up with BASELINE_2026-08-06_render_audit.txt. Note
-- orchestration_states reaps terminal rows at ~24h, so "0 rows" the next day
-- means "not in the last day", not "never ran" — ask scheduled_tasks, which
-- has no reaper.

grounded_in: content_components.html_template, live row `case-studies-grid`, read 2026-08-06: `.csg-cta-btn { background: var(--color-accent, var(--color-secondary)); color: var(--color-primary-text, #fff); }`. finetuning.uk's served /assets/css/styles.css defines BOTH: `--color-accent: #C8873A` and `--color-primary-text: #ffffff`. So the #fff fallback never fires and nothing is hard-coded — the component names the ink slot for a PRIMARY fill while filling with ACCENT. This REFUTES my round-1 description of this failure as 'a component hard-coding an ink over a themed fill'.

gaswholesalers.com served stylesheet, line 109, the base element rule: `a { color: var(--color-accent); }` with `--color-accent: #E8A020` on a white page = 2.22:1, six occurrences — every one of that site's failures. It is in the LAYOUT css_template, not a component, and accent here is an ink, not a fill. --color-accent-text (ink ON an accent fill) is the wrong direction for it; this is what forced the third variable.

gamesdesign.co.uk: `system-stats` .stats-eyebrow is `color: var(--color-accent, #7dd3fc); background: var(--section-surface);`. Served values --color-accent #00e5ff, --section-surface rgba(255,255,255,0.05), --color-primary #00bcd4. The audit's measured backdrop rgb(13,191,214) is exactly 0.05*255 + 0.95*[0,188,212] = [12.75, 191.35, 214.15], which identifies the section fill as `primary` arithmetically rather than by assumption. 1.44:1.

MEASURED 2026-08-06, the round-1 finding that still stands: 0 of 18 layouts contain `palette "accent_text"` while 18 of 18 contain `palette "primary_text"`; and `--color-accent-text` appears 0 times across content_components, layouts, css_snippets, site_components and page_components. Confirmed at the other end too — grep of the three failing sites' SERVED stylesheets returns 0 definitions of --color-accent-text and 0 of --color-primary-ink. The slot is derived by the platform and consumed by nothing.

LANDMINES.md, from this bug's own dartsonline round: 'A palette slot no LAYOUT declares is never emitted — deriving it is dead config.' This is why emission is renderer-owned. palette_specialised_slots.go:75-94 records the same lesson in code, having caught icon_chip_bg before it shipped: 'I added it, then measured, and it would have been dead config — the exact shape that looks live and is not.'

render_css_from_spec_action.go:699-721, buildTokenAliases: 'returns a :root block defining every tokenAliases name that is not already DEFINED anywhere in css. A definition is the name followed by a colon ("--shadow:"), which cannot match a var() usage.' buildLegibleInkDefaults is a third instance of this established renderer-owned pattern (buildSectionDefaults step 10, buildTokenAliases step 11), not a new mechanism — and inherits the same order dependency, which edit 6 now asserts instead of describing.

palette_specialised_slots.go:288-308 (pickInkOn) and color_util.go:134-162 (pickReadableOnBackground), both read in full for this round rather than described. Each takes exactly one bgHex; each walks a fixed preference list; neither can return the colour it was asked about, because neither is ever asked about one — they are handed a GROUND and asked for an ink. That is the prior_art_librarian's LOW objection answered by reading the bodies, which is what it asked for.

SCOPED OUT, MEASURED: 47 of 173 active unforked content_components declare a renderer-owned --section-* token, 32 of them with a raw rgb/rgba literal — against the renderer's own emitted contract, visible in every served stylesheet: 'Themes MUST NOT declare --section-* defaults; the renderer owns this.' system-stats' `.system-stats-section { --section-text-muted: rgba(255,255,255,0.7) }` is why gamesdesign shows 8 failures at 1.72:1 that this plan does NOT fix, and brief-explanation is why idea.uk shows 14. ~22 of the 109. Filed as its own bug rather than folded in — it is an unenforced contract, not a missing variable.

BASELINE_2026-08-06_render_audit.txt, banked before any change: 15 pages, 109 contrast failures, browser-measured (headless Chromium, computed style, alpha-composited backdrop). NOTE the baseline as first banked covered only 10 sites / 82 failures and was MISSING dartsonline and robot-hands — the two sub-shape A sites this plan targets — so it could not have verified its own fix. Completed this round: dartsonline 1 (.image-hover-card-grid__eyebrow 1.04), robot-hands 3 (.tl-card-link 1.07, .tl-eyebrow 1.14), vonc 23, relojistas 0, vetcomparison 0.

The 090 diagnosis for ai-agent-orchestration.com's 30 failures (correlation 5853ee07-a49c-4571-8ea0-3eb660e43dfd) returned status UNVERIFIABLE: 'Diagnosis NOT confirmed (stopped: iteration-cap). Best-effort trail attached for a human; no fix proposed.' Five bundles, no cause established. That site is untouched by this plan and is NOT claimed as fixed by it.
plan.risks:
1. THE SCHEME WIDENING, unchanged from round 1 and still the thing to push on.
fillDarkSchemeSpecialisedSlots is dark-only by a deliberate, documented boundary
('a light literal is only wrong when the site is dark'). buildLegibleInkDefaults
deliberately does not adopt it, because two of the three accent-direction sites are
LIGHT (gaswholesalers #F4F1EB, finetuning #F5F3EF) and a dark-only guard cannot
reach them at all. Round 1: architecture rated this LOW and asked that it be
RECORDED so a future narrowing does not silently stop covering its own measured
cases; guardian rated it LOW and asked for human sign-off rather than blocking. It
is recorded in the concept-register entry shipping in the same commit, and test
case 4 fails loudly if someone re-narrows it. I am flagging it a second time
because a reviewer blessing it in round 1's context may not have been blessing a
THIRD variable.

2. A THIRD VARIABLE IS MORE THAN ROUND 1 ASKED FOR. --color-accent-ink is new
surface that no seat has reviewed. It is the same shape as --color-primary-ink,
measured unused across all five surfaces before naming, and inert until a template
opts in — but it did not exist when the panel last looked, so it should be read as
new rather than as a detail of an approved plan.

3. WHAT THIS PLAN DOES NOT FIX, stated as a count so the arithmetic is checkable.
109 measured failures. This closes 12 (dartsonline 1, robot-hands 2, finetuning 2,
gaswholesalers 6, gamesdesign 1) plus .stats-eyebrow on vonc. It does not touch:
ai-agent-orchestration 30 (diagnosis UNVERIFIABLE, needs a human), vonc's 22
gauntlet failures (gauntlet_dead_cta lane owns that surface), the ~22
--section-*-override failures across gamesdesign and idea.uk (its own bug), and the
over-image approximations the audit itself marks as not firm. A reader who takes
'contrast bug fixed' from this plan would be wrong, which is why the number is here.

4. THE MIGRATION TOUCHES FLEET-SHARED TEMPLATES. 4 components and 5 of 18 layouts.
Owning pipeline named at the edit (brochure_component_library). The var() fallback
is what makes it safe to apply before every stylesheet has re-rendered, and every
replacement preserves today's exact value as the fallback — but system-stats and the
layouts' `a {}` rule reach well beyond the sites measured here, so the blast radius
is larger than the failure count. It is bounded by inertness, not by scope.

5. PROPAGATION IS A SEPARATE STEP AND IS EASY TO CALL DONE TOO EARLY. The migration
changes source templates; stored page_components keep the old markup until a scoped
rerender. A completed migration, a completed rerender work item and a green row
count are all compatible with an unchanged live page. Verification is the served
page re-audited against the banked baseline, and the Go half is verified by grepping
the RUNNING POD for a string this change adds plus a negative control, not by the
tag and not by git.

6. THE COUNT ITSELF IS A WEAK VERIFIER. A falling failure count is content-dependent
— 122's own dartsonline round found the same defect reporting 1 or 2 depending which
cards a page happened to render. The strong check is per-selector: the named
selectors at the named ratios are gone, and no new selector has appeared.

7. NOT IN THIS SUBMISSION, IN THE SAME COMMIT: the concept-register entry (condition
(2) of the 2026-07-29 ordering exemption, which stands) and a LANDMINE for the
two-grounds constraint. Named here so their absence from the edit list is not read
as an omission.
